q: 1. The best method of interpolation of contours, is by
explain: Graphical interpolation (using a series of parallel equally-spaced lines or a tracing paper method) is the most accurate and commonly preferred method of interpolating contour points.

q: 2. For preparation of contour plan for a route survey
options: method of trace contour is used
method of cross profile is used
indirect method of contouring is used
explain: For route surveys (roads, railways), contour plans are prepared using cross-sections taken perpendicular to the centre line, i.e., the method of cross profile.

q: 3. Accuracy of elevation of various points obtained from contour map is limited to
explain: The accuracy of elevations read from a contour map is generally limited to about half (1/2) of the contour interval, since contours are drawn at discrete intervals.

q: 4. The constant vertical distance between two adjacent contours, is called
explain: The constant difference of elevation between two consecutive contour lines is termed the contour interval.

q: 5. The V-shaped contour represents
explain: Contours crossing a stream or depression form V-shapes pointing upstream (toward higher ground), representing a valley; a ridge would show contours pointing away from higher ground (downhill).

q: 6. Straight, parallel and widely spaced contours represent
explain: Evenly, widely-spaced and straight/parallel contours indicate a uniformly sloping (inclined plane) surface; closely spaced contours indicate steep ground, and widely spaced but irregular contours indicate flatter, gently undulating ground.

q: 7. Contours of different elevations may cross each other only in the case of
explain: Normally contours of different elevations never cross; the sole exception is an overhanging cliff or cave, where the ground surface doubles back on itself, allowing contours of different elevations to appear to cross in plan.

q: 8. Closed contours of decreasing values towards their centre, represent
explain: When the innermost closed contour has the lowest elevation value, the feature represents a depression (a hollow); a hill is represented by closed contours of increasing value towards the centre.

q: 9. An imaginary line lying throughout on the surface of the earth and preserving a constant inclination to the horizontal, is called
explain: A line on the ground surface that maintains a constant inclination (gradient) to the horizontal throughout is called a contour gradient (grade contour), unlike a contour line which is horizontal (constant elevation).

q: 10. Deviation of the actual road gradient from the proposed contour gradient up hill side involves
options: earth work on the centre line
explain: When the actual road alignment on the uphill side deviates from (cuts across, rising faster than) the contour gradient, the road surface lies below the natural ground, requiring excavation along the centre line.

q: 11. The method generally preferred to for contouring an undulating area is,
explain: Tacheometric surveying, which can quickly determine both horizontal and vertical distances/elevations from a single setup, is best suited for contouring an undulating (hilly, uneven) area.

q: 12. Bergchund is a topographical feature in
explain: Bergchund/bergschrund-type terrain features are associated with hilly/mountainous topography, as per the book's classification.

q: 13. The relief representation on the map can be depicted
explain: Relief (terrain relief) on a map can be shown using multiple methods - spot levels, altitude tinting/layers, and hill shading - so all of the above apply.

q: 14. The suitable contour interval for a map with scale 1 : 10000 is
explain: For a relatively large scale map such as 1:10000, a fine contour interval of about 2 m is typically suitable to show ground detail adequately.

q: 15. Which of the following methods of contouring is most suitable for hilly terrain?
explain: The tacheometric method of contouring is most suitable for hilly terrain because it quickly provides both horizontal distance and elevation to numerous points without the need for chaining across difficult ground.

q: 16. A series of closely spaced contour lines represents a
explain: Closely spaced contour lines indicate a rapid change in elevation over a short horizontal distance, representing a steep slope.

q: 17. An imaginary line lying throughout on the surface of the earth and preserving a constant inclination to the horizontal, is called
explain: A contour gradient is an imaginary line on the ground surface that maintains a constant inclination (slope) to the horizontal throughout its length.

q: 18. From any point on the surface with a given inclination
options: only one contour gradient is possible
explain: From any given point with a specified inclination, two contour gradients are geometrically possible - one running in each direction around the slope at that constant grade.

q: 19. Location of contour gradient for a highway is best set out from
explain: For highway alignment, the contour gradient is best set out starting from a saddle (low point on a ridge) and working down the hill, providing more efficient routing options.

q: 20. Contours are used to determine
options: indivisibility of points on a contour map
area of the drainage basin and capacity of the reservoir
explain: Contour maps are versatile tools used to determine intervisibility of points, drainage basin areas and reservoir capacities, and earthwork quantities, so all listed uses apply.

q: 21. The vertical distance between any two consecutive contours is called
explain: The constant vertical distance between any two consecutive contour lines on a map is, by definition, the contour interval.

q: 22. The horizontal distance between any two consecutive contours is called
explain: The horizontal distance between two consecutive contours (which varies with the slope) is called the horizontal equivalent.

q: 23. An imaginary line on the surface of the earth having a constant inclination with the horizontal (slope) is called
explain: As defined earlier, an imaginary line on the ground maintaining a constant slope (inclination to horizontal) is called a contour gradient.

q: 24. Contour lines cross ridge or valley lines at
explain: As established earlier, contour lines always cross ridge lines and valley lines at right angles (90 degrees), since these lines represent the direction of steepest slope.

q: 25. Contour interval is
options: inversely proportional to the scale of the map
directly proportional to the flatness of ground
larger if the time available is more
explain: A larger map scale (more detailed) generally uses a smaller contour interval and vice versa, so the contour interval is inversely proportional to the scale of the map.

q: 26. In indirect method of contouring, the best method of interpolation of contours is
explain: Interpolating contour positions between spot levels by arithmetical (proportional) calculation is considered the most accurate method, though graphical and estimation methods are quicker alternatives.

q: 27. The constant vertical distance between two adjacent contours, is called
explain: The constant vertical distance between two adjacent contours on a map is, by definition, the contour interval.

q: 28. Two contour lines, having the same may cross each other only in the case of
explain: Two contour lines of the same elevation can unite (coincide/merge) together in special cases such as at a vertical cliff, though they do not typically cross transversely.

q: 29. In route surveys, the most suitable method of contouring is
explain: For route surveys (roads, railways), the cross-section method of contouring is most suitable, since cross-sections perpendicular to the alignment naturally provide the elevation data needed for design.

q: 30. A pass or a saddle in a mountainous region
options: the lowest point of the ridge lines coincides with the highest point of the valley point
explain: A pass/saddle in mountainous terrain is characterized by all these features together - it lies between two ridge lines, connects two valleys, and represents the point where the lowest point of the ridge meets the highest point of the intervening valley - so all of these apply.

q: 31. In indirect method of contouring, the best method of interpolation if contours
explain: For the indirect method of contouring, contour interpolation between spot levels can be done using any of these methods - graphical, estimation, or arithmetical calculation - so all of these are valid.
